So, but I think the playmaking and making your teammates better, that's something you can take with you at every step of your career.

quotes.speaker: Ray Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Felton on how the NBA has changed for point guards since 2005
quotes.excerpt: The game is definitely changed from when we first came in the league in 2005.
quotes.quote: The game is definitely changed from when we first came in the league in 2005. You had to be a traditional point guard because you had legit centers. You used to run a lot of floppy. You had to throw that ball in the post and you had to get guys involved. Like, you know, it was just what it was. You had legit bonafide scorers on your team. If you didn't get them the rock, they were going to let your ass know. And that's just what it was. But at the same time, you know, we still had to be scoring point guards, too, because you couldn't be a liability on the court. You know, that shit would get exposed back then. But now, traditional point guards are the Steph Currys and, you know, the Kyries and the, you know, Shai, Lucas, who give you 30 a night. You know, so the game is different.

quotes.excerpt: The lack of teaching guys how to be true point guards, those days are over.
quotes.quote: We were talking about the lack of teaching guys how to be true point guards. Those days are over because we are watching the Shais. No offense to those guys, they are doing what they are asked to do for their perspective teams, but it is hindering the youth because they feel like they have to do that, but they are not that. So when that is the case, if you are not scoring and you are not helping your teammates by winning and being better and helping them get easy shots, what are you at that point?

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton on the individualization of basketball training
quotes.excerpt: Any training in basketball is now individualized. They are not teaching, 'Hey, come off the screen and roll.'
quotes.quote: First of all, any training in basketball is now individualized. They are not teaching, 'Hey, come off the screen and roll, look at the pocket pass, or come off the screen and roll, split the double and then kick to the corner.' That is not being taught in an actual training session. We might be teaching our kids that, but nobody else is. And one is because a lot of guys can teach NBA basketball or NBA reads or that type of basketball. Why? Because they did not play NBA basketball so they do not know what coaches or anybody else is kind of looking for. All they have been taught their whole life is to go one-on-one, go try to score the basketball, do this, do that, but not, 'Hey, you got to get your team involved.'

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the loss of team-based basketball in youth development
quotes.excerpt: When we were coming up, if we wanted to play, we were going to get six people, we were going to play three-on-three.
quotes.quote: When we were coming up, if we wanted to play, we were going to get six people, we were going to play three-on-three. We were going to play two-on-two. Kids do not do that no more. Kids are not just going to hoop. I would go to the rec center and I am 12 years old, I am playing with grown-ass men and it, you know, like that. Kids do not do that no more. I always played two age groups up. Always played two age groups up. My AAU team was placing in the 17 under nationals at 15 years old.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on youth players reclassifying to be the best
quotes.excerpt: You do see way more kids nowadays playing their age group or reclassing and playing down.
quotes.quote: You do see way more kids nowadays playing their age group or reclassing and playing down. Because they want to be the best. Perfect example, I just had, so my 12-year-old son, he does not mind playing, right? We are thinking about like reclassing him to his actual grade because he still, he literally just turned 13. So, he, we are talking about reclassing him back to his actual grade, but they had an opportunity to play in the sixth-grade level even though they are seventh grade or whatever with a bunch of reclasses, but I told them, I said, 'Y'all should play and take the opportunity to play eighth grade, play up a grade.' My son was like, 'Yeah, I am playing,' and maybe two other kids, but the rest of the kids were like, 'Nah, I am good.' I was like, 'That is weak.' You want to go down and beat on some younger kids for clips, but you do not want to get better. You do not get better playing older kids. Take your chances and see and shock the world.
